title: Nvidia’s Earnings on Deck; Anthropic’s Public Debut
summary: If life was simple, the biggest question this week for people in tech would be where Anthropic shares open when the AI firm goes public. (Above $150 a share? See below.) Instead, we can’t rule out that more news breaks in the Nvidia drama and overwhelms Anthropic’s week in the sun. That news could be anything from reports of other women who had affairs with the now-departed CEO, Jensen Huang to developments inthe campaigntobring him back.Huang, meanwhile, hasagreed to testifybefore Congress, which could happen this week.Of course, even without such developments, Nvidia will be in the news. The AI chip designer on Tuesday is scheduled to report earnings for its third fiscal quarter, ending in late October. Those earnings will remind us all of why it is such a star company: It has projected revenue growth of around 89%, continuing a reacceleration of growth this fiscal year from last year’s “slowdown” (when revenue grew 66%). What we’ll be focused on more than the numbers will be comments from Nvidia’s interim CEO, Colette Kress. While as finance chief she’s a fixture on these calls, on Tuesday she makes her first public appearance in charge of the company since Huang’s exit.
title_es: Nvidia reporta resultados; Anthropic debuta en bolsa
bajada: Esta semana Nvidia reporta ganancias con crecimiento proyectado de 89%, mientras Anthropic hace su debut público. El drama de la renuncia de Jensen Huang y potenciales nuevas revelaciones podrían dominar la cobertura.
bajada_en: This week Nvidia reports earnings with projected 89% revenue growth, while Anthropic makes its public debut. The drama of Jensen Huang's resignation and potential new revelations could dominate coverage.

title: alibaba /open-code-review
summary: OpenCodeReview English | 简体中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Русский What is Open Code Review? Open Code Review is an AI-powered code review CLI tool. It originated as Alibaba Group's internal official AI code review assistant — over the past two years, it has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. After thorough validation at massive scale, we incubated it into an open source project for the community. Simply configure a model endpoint to get started. It reads Git diffs, sends changed files to a configurable LLM via an agent with tool-use capabilities, and generates structured review comments with line-level precision. The agent can read full file contents, search the codebase, inspect other changed files for context, and produce deep reviews — not just surface-level diff feedback. Beyond diff review, ocr scan reviews entire files for auditing unfamiliar codebases or directories that have no meaningful diff. Visit the official website for more details. Benchmark Compared to general-purpose agents (Claude Code), Open Code Review achieves significantly higher Precision and F1 with the same underlying model, while consuming only ~1/9 of the tokens and completing reviews faster. Note that its Recall is lower than general-purpose agents — a deliberate trade-off favoring precision over noise. A real-world code review benchmark built from 50 popular open-source repositories, 200 real Pull Requests, and 10 programming languages — cross-validated by 80+ senior engineers ( 1,505 annotated ground-truth issues). Explore the AACR-Bench dataset on Hugging Face . Metric What it measures Why it matters F1 Harmonic mean of precision and recall Best single number for overall review quality Precision Proportion of reported issues that are real defects Higher = fewer false alarms to triage Recall Proportion of real defects that are found Higher = fewer issues slip through review Avg Time Wall-clock time per review Matters for CI pipeline latency Avg Token Total

title: [Meta FAIR + NYU] Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding: training 200+ MLLMs to find encoder pretraining is optional but vision-only parameters are not [R]
summary: X threads (with videos!):https://x.com/choang333/status/2121335484236386574https://x.com/_ellisbrown/status/2121335477244428419Paper:https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.17334Blog and FAQ:https://unbundling.github.ioLabs disagree on vision encoders right now.Gemma 4 12B dropped the encoder, Kimi K3 trains its encoder from scratch, and Inkling 2 Small brought an encoder back. Published models can't settle this, because they differ in data and compute and rarely account for encoder pretraining. A standard encoder also bundles three choices: separate pretraining, parameters that only vision tokens use, and placement before the LLM. We tested each choice separately.Setup:200+ models, all trained from scratch (LLM included) on the same data.Lifetime compute: encoder pretraining counts against the same budget as multimodal training.Main comparisons use Qwen3-1.7B and 4B configurations with 0.4B parameters of vision capacity. A scaling ladder covers 0.6B to 6.4B backbone sizes.Evaluations are on 16 VQA benchmarks from Cambrian at 448 px. and 12 language benchmarks testing commonsense, QA, and broad knowledge.Findings:Separate pretraining is optional.Encoders pretrained with four objectives (contrastive, self-supervised, two captioning) at best tie an encoder trained from scratch with the LLM at matched compute. Even free pretraining doesn't help. Pretraining MetaCLIP 6.5x longer raised ImageNet linear-probe accuracy (80.4% → 84.4%) but not VQA.Vision-only parameters are required.Encoder-free models trail at every size from 0.6B to 6.4B and need about 3x the compute to catch up. Giving the LLM the encoder's parameters instead improves text, not VQA.Placement before the LLM is optional."In-fusion" adds zero-initialized vision-only weights (attention projections and FFNs) to the LLM's first 8 layers, and text tokens never use them. It's on par with the encoder from 1.7B to 6.4B, with about 13% lower time to first token. At 1.7B, vision-only branches in layers 1–8 reach 45.0 VQA
title_es: Meta y NYU estudian componentes críticos en modelos multimodales
bajada: Investigadores de Meta FAIR y NYU entrenaron 200+ modelos para determinar qué partes de visión son esenciales. El estudio concluye que preentrenamiento de encoder es opcional pero parámetros vision-only no.
bajada_en: Meta FAIR and NYU researchers trained 200+ models to determine essential vision components. The study finds that encoder pretraining is optional but vision-only parameters are not.

title: Tencent /LoopForge

LoopForge is a self-hosted workspace where your team ships software with coding agents. Describe what you need to Main Bot in chat: it opens a Docker sandbox, checks out your repositories, delegates to project roles, and opens the PR. When a way of working proves itself, save it as an SOP (a standard workflow of agents, scripts and human gates) so the next requirement is delivered the same way, with review and approval built in. Coding-agent CLIs do the work: CodeBuddy, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Antigravity, Kimi Code, Pi, DeepSeek Harness and ZCode. LoopForge adds the roles, sandboxes, checkpoints and history around them, all on your own infrastructure under the MIT license. title: ag-ui-protocol /ag-ui
summary:
AG-UI: The Agent-User Interaction Protocol AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.
Built for simplicity and flexibility, it enables seamless integration between AI agents, real time user context, and user interfaces. Join our Discord → Read the Docs → Go to the AG-UI Dojo → Follow us → 🚀 Getting Started Create a new AG-UI application in seconds: npx create-ag-ui-app my-agent-app Useful Links: The AG-UI Dojo Build AG-UI-powered applications(Quickstart) Build new AG-UI framework integrations (Quickstart) Book a call to discuss an AG-UI integration with a new framework Join the Discord Community What is AG-UI? AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol for agent-human interaction, designed for simplicity & flexibility: During agent executions, agent backends emit events compatible with one of AG-UI's ~16 standard event types Agent backends can accept one of a few simple AG-UI compatible inputs as arguments AG-UI includes a flexible middleware layer that ensures compatibility across diverse environments: Works with any event transport (SSE, WebSockets, webhooks, etc.) Allows for loose event format matching , enabling broad agent and app interoperability It also ships with a reference HTTP implementation and default connector to help teams get started fast. Learn more about the specs → Why AG-UI? AG-UI was developed based on real-world requirements and practical experience building in-app agent interactions. Where does AGUI fit in the agentic protocol stack? AG-UI is complementary to the other 2 top agentic protocols MCP gives agents tools A2A allows agents to communicate with other agents AG-UI brings agents into user-facing applications 🚀 Features 💬 Real-time agentic chat with streaming 🔄 Bi-directional state synchronization 🧩 Generative UI and structured messages 🧠 Real-time context enrichment 🛠️ Frontend tool integration 🧑‍💻 Human-in-the-loop collaboration 🛠 Supported Integratio
title_es: AG-UI: protocolo estándar para agentes y aplicaciones

title: ggml-org /ggml
summary:
ggml Tensor library for machine learning Quick start Build from source: git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml cd ggml

mkdir build && cd build

Plain C/C++ implementation without any dependencies Cross-platform - x86, ARM, RISC-V, LoongArch, PowerPC, s390x, and WebAssembly SIMD-optimized kernels for x86, ARM, and RISC-V Broad backend support - CPU, GPU, NPU, and browser 2- to 8-bit integer quantization, plus MXFP4 and NVFP4 microscaling formats Zero memory allocations during runtime Documentation The GGUF file format Introduction to ggml GGML tips & tricks Contributing For changes to the core ggml library (including to the CMake build system), please open a PR in llama.cpp - doing so will make your PR more visible, better tested, and more likely to be reviewed

title: dream-num /univer
summary: Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK. Start with open-source Sheets and Docs, then connect your own application or agent. 🚀 Quick start · 📚 Documentation · ⚖️ Feature comparison · 🌐 Website · 🎮 Showcase · 🔧 API Reference · 📝 Blog English · Français · Deutsch · Español · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 Table of contents 💡 What is Univer? Open-source capabilities 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor Connect your application to editable content 🏗️ Explore the open-source architecture Give custom features clear boundaries Compose cross-feature edits and undo/redo Connect applications and agents through Facade APIs and events 🧩 Extend your application with Univer Office SDK Scope and licensing 🌐 Application patterns and ecosystem Univer Workspace: an Office SDK reference application CLI, agent integrations, and developer skills 📚 Documentation and contributing Runtime compatibility 💬 Community 🔒 Security ❤️ Sponsors 📄 License 💡 What is Univer? Univer is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs. Univer Office SDK has three parts: Web SDK is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor. Server SDK adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export. AI SDK connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations. This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementation
